text: Most candidates prepare the wrong thing.
Most of the files in your pool come from consulting and banking.
Few candidates name a cost. A few of them name two.
Hardly any file gets an argument, and hardly any of them reach a third reader.
Most of the files in that pool come from consulting and banking. Mine does not.
Hardly any applicant in my year has signed off on a concrete pour at six in the morning.
Few of my decisions are made alone, but the ones that cost money are.
I am below the threshold on goals, and I know exactly what offsets it.
None of the six criteria is about my title, and that is good news for me.

People imagine a room, and there is a room, but it comes later. What happens first is a sheet with six criteria on it and a number under each one, and two of us read your file against it separately. Most of the differences between the two of us are half a point. Now, the part candidates get wrong: the six lines are not equal, and they are not added up. Progression and scope of responsibility carry more weight than anything else, and the test score carries the least. A few programs here have stopped asking for it. What I am doing is weighing one line against another, so a low number in one place is not a problem if something in the file offsets it. And the files that worry me are the ones with no low number anywhere. Almost all of them look the same: good grades, good employer, good English, and nothing I can remember by Friday.

I was rejected the first year and admitted the second, with a better job in between, and I do not think the job is what changed it. The first time, five of my six answers were fine. The sixth one, the one about what I would bring to the class, I answered with ambition. I wrote about what I wanted to learn. Hardly any of that is useful to a committee, because every file in the pool wants to learn. The second time I wrote about the thing none of them had. I had rebuilt a factory line in a country where I did not speak the language, and I named the two months when it nearly failed. Most of my file did not change at all. One paragraph changed, and it was the paragraph that told them what the class would lose if I were not in it.
